statement: Equal triangles which are on equal bases and on the same side are also in the same parallels.
heath_proof: Let ABC, CDE be equal triangles on equal bases BC, CE and on the same side. I say that they are also in the same parallels. For let AD be joined; I say that AD is parallel to BE. For, if not, let AF be drawn through A parallel to BE [I. 31], and let FE be joined. Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE; for they are on equal bases BC, CE and in the same parallels BE, AF. [I. 38] But the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DCE; therefore the triangle DCE is also equal to the triangle FCE, [C. N. 1]the greater to the less: which is impossible. Therefore AF is not parallel to BE. Similarly we can prove that neither is any other straight line except AD; therefore AD is parallel to BE.
ai_proof_text:
1.40
**Statement:** Equal triangles which are on equal bases and on the same side are also in the same parallels.

**Step 1.** Let ABC and DCE be equal triangles on the equal bases BC and CE, where B, C, E lie in one straight line BE, and let the vertices A and D lie on the same side of BE. Join AD [P1]. I say that AD is parallel to BE, so that the two triangles are in the same parallels BE, AD.

**Step 2.** Suppose, if possible, that AD is not parallel to BE. Through the point A draw the straight line AF parallel to BE [1.31]. Since AD is not parallel to BE, the line AF is distinct from AD, and the two lines AF, AD have only the point A in common.

**Step 3.** The straight line DC meets BE at C. The line DC, produced if necessary, must meet AF: for if it did not, then DC and AF, being produced indefinitely and never meeting, would be parallel [D1.23]; then DC and BE, being each parallel to AF, would be parallel to one another [1.30], which is impossible because DC meets BE at C. Let DC, produced if necessary, meet AF at the point F. The point F is distinct from D, for otherwise AF would pass through A and D and so coincide with AD. Join FE [P1].

**Step 4.** The triangle ABC is on the base BC, the triangle FCE is on the base CE, the bases BC and CE are equal, and both triangles lie in the same parallels BE and AF (their bases on BE, their vertices A and F on AF). Therefore the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle FCE [1.38].

**Step 5.** But the triangle ABC is equal to the triangle DCE by hypothesis. Therefore the triangle DCE is equal to the triangle FCE [CN1].

**Step 6.** Now F and D are distinct points of the straight line DC on the same side of BE as A (since AF, being parallel to BE, never crosses BE). Hence either F lies between D and C, in which case the triangle FCE is a part of the triangle DCE, or D lies between F and C, in which case the triangle DCE is a part of the triangle FCE. In either case one of the two triangles is a part of the other, and the whole is greater than the part [CN5]; so the triangles DCE and FCE are unequal, which contradicts Step 5.

**Step 7.** Therefore the supposition of Step 2 is impossible, and AD is parallel to BE. Hence the equal triangles ABC and DCE, being on the equal bases BC and CE and on the same side of BE, are in the same parallels BE and AD. Q.E.D.
